sections.text: Introduction

The purpose of this procedure is to provide detailed
 instructions on a safe method for replacing V string insulators on 220KV
 Suspension towers.

This procedure was developed by EEC engineers in head
 office and zones using documentation from Ontario Hydro information System and
 adapted to meet EECs needs.
Safety Precautions

items: A work permit must be issued.
Local earthing on both sides of the work is required.

Wear your 
safety helmet, safety belts.

Wear your 
safety helmet, safety belts.

sections.text: Safety Summary

The following hazards and precautions are emphasized to
highlight some of the safety considerations related to this job.

Other hazards, which are, site specific and of a general
nature must be identified during the tailboard conference before the work
commences.

Test the conductor for isolation and apply earths to the conductor in
 procedures.

items:
Test the conductor for isolation and apply earths to the conductor in
 procedures.
Maintain clearance from any adjacent energized circuits
Calculate the conductor weight to determine the load on the rigging.
Inspect the condition of the tools and equipment before use.
Remain clear of the insulators while they are being lowered.
Wear approved fall protection.
Good verbal communication is required of all crew members

Work to be Carried Out
Preliminary Work

items:
Install the capstan hoist on the leg of the tower in a position that will
 allow the equipment to be raised and lowered.

Attach the handline to the tower arm or leg in a convenient location to
 raise the equipment.

Test the conductor for isolation and apply earths using approved earthing
 procedures.

Attach a rope ladder to the tower arm for access to the lower end of
 insulator strings.

sections.text:
Replacing the insulators using a basket-type
sling
Lower the insulators to the ground and replace the defective units.

The insulator string may have to be directed away from any
 conductor or tower arms below the work site as it is being lowered.

items:
Install the nylon lifting sling on the two bottom arm angles of
 the arm directly above the conductor and then attach the chain-hoist to the
 lower V ring on the lifting sling

Install the 16 mm (5/8 in) shackle into the hole in the steel yoke
 supporting the conductor and insert the chain hook of the hoist into the
 shackle. See figure 2. TO accommodate the hoist hook a larger shackle can be
 attached to the first shackle if required.
Take up on the hoist to slacken the insulator strings.

Attach the handline or a short piece of rope to the bottom of the
 insulator string.

Hitch the rope over the conductor to allow the insulators to swing to a
 vertical position after the string has been disconnected.

Attach a snatch block to the arm above the insulator string using a nylon
 sling.

Install a snatch block on the tower shaft at the arm angle connection also
 using a nylon sling and then insert the lifting rope through both snatch
 blocks. See Figure 3.

Attach the insulator lifting yoke to the end of the rope and then install
 the yoke on the first or second unit from the top of the string. See Figure
 3.

Take the weight of the insulator string on the rope using the capstan
 hoist and disconnect the insulator string from the tower arm.
Lower the insulators to the ground and replace the defective units.

Check the insulator sockets and keys for proper positioning while
 replacing the units in the string.
Reverse the procedure to raise and reconnect the insulator string.

Disconnect and relocate the rope and snatch blocks if there are insulator
 units in the other string that require replacement.

Disconnect the equipment from the tower and then remove and lower the
 earths.
Surrender the work protection on the circuit.

Alternative Method

items:
Install a sling on the tower arm
 adjacent to the insulator attachment hardware and then insert the chain hook
 of the hoist into the lower eye of the sling.

Attach a nylon sling or conductor
 lifting shoe to the conductor adjacent to the clamp and insert the hook on the
 body end of the chain hoist into it. See Figure 3.

Take up on the hoist to slacken the
 insulator string.

When only the bottom units are to be
 replaced. Lash the lower insulator units to the chain hoist.

Remove the defective units from the
 string and lower them to the ground.

Raise the replacement insulators and
 insert them into the string.

Check that all the insulator sockets
 and keys are properly positioned before removing the lashing ropes.

Disconnect and lower the equipment or
 relocate it to the other string if it contains insulator units that require
 replacement.

When the complete string or the upper
 units require replacement, the insulator string can be disconnected and
 lowered to the ground using the method outlined in the procedure.
